name: Thoradin's Wall
summary: At Thoradin's Wall, broken stone divides the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. King Thoradin ordered it built long ago to shield early humanity from Amani troll incursions.

sections.title: A Bulwark of Ancient Arathor
sections.body: Thoradin's Wall once guarded Strom's western frontier. Nearly three thousand years ago, King Thoradin raised it across the valley corridor to shield humanity's young settlements from Amani forest troll raids. Strom stood at the heart of Arathor, the first unified human empire. The wall protected its heartland, giving humanity room to survive and challenge troll supremacy in the north.

sections.title: Centuries of Decay
sections.body: Thoradin's Wall now lies in severe disrepair. Great breaches split its ramparts, worn down by weather, warfare, and abandonment. Arathor splintered into rival kingdoms, and neighboring Lordaeron later fell to the Scourge. No central realm remains to maintain the masonry. Travelers and roaming bandits pass freely through the broken archways between Hillsbrad and the untamed Arathi Highlands.

faq.answer: King Thoradin commissioned Thoradin's Wall nearly three thousand years ago. He unified humanity's tribes and founded the Empire of Arathor.

faq.q: Why was the wall built in the first place?
faq.answer: King Thoradin ordered Thoradin's Wall built to defend Strom, humanity's early capital, and its fledgling settlements from raids by the neighboring Amani troll empire.

faq.q: Why is the wall so broken down today?
faq.answer: Thousands of years of weathering, conflict, and neglect have broken down Thoradin's Wall. After Arathor splintered into independent human nations, the frontier fortification lost its strategic priority and fell into disrepair.

faq.q: What regions does Thoradin's Wall separate?
faq.answer: Thoradin's Wall separates the Hillsbrad Foothills to the west from the Arathi Highlands to the east.

angles.text: As a human, you stand before Thoradin's Wall and face human antiquity in the enduring masonry of King Thoradin, who first unified the scattered human tribes.
As a troll, you see in these ruined fortifications the trace of ancient territorial wars, when humanity halted the forest trolls' domain.
